one_sentence_story: Watch a short silent clip of a stranger scratching an arm. Most adults soon itch on clean skin as the brain fires a bug alarm.
so_what_for_you: Do not rake your nails when a sudden itch hits. Press a cool flat palm on the spot for ten seconds.

jargon_map.plain: Feeling a real skin itch just from seeing someone else scratch.
jargon_map.analogy: Like your skin running a bug drill when a friend flinches.

jargon_map.plain: A deep brain fold that tracks gut state, heat, and skin itch.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a warning light on your car dash.

jargon_map.plain: How fast your nerves tense up around stress or small threats.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a smoke alarm set way too high.

jargon_map.plain: Scratching feels good for one second. Right after, it makes the skin itch worse.
jargon_map.analogy: Like pouring salt water on thirst.
